content.text:
I am the breath made meaningful, the vibration given purpose. I am the bridge between the isolated mind and the world beyond it.

I emerge from silence and return to it. In between, I carry everything—love, rage, wonder, deception, prayer. I can wound deeper than any blade or heal what seemed unhealable.

I am older than writing, older than cities. I lived first in caves, in warning cries, in the naming of fire. Every child reaches for me, shaping mouth and tongue until I finally come, that first word, and nothing is ever the same.

I am never the thought itself—only its shadow, its approximation. This is my tragedy. The speaker knows what they meant; the listener knows only what they heard. In the gap between us, worlds are lost. Wars begin. Love fails.

Yet still you speak. Still you try.

I can be silenced by power, by fear, by the hand over the mouth. But I am stubborn. I find ways. I become whisper, become code, become the words mouthed across a room.

I am happening now, in this very moment, though I wear the strange mask of text. You hear me anyway, don't you? A voice in your mind that is somehow yours and somehow not.

Speak me.

I exist only when you do.
